Title: Thoughts Betrayed vs Muddled Vampire Hunter

Messages.Author: hel...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
Scenario:

Samson has 2 blood, and is attacked by a Muddled Vampire Hunter.

He plays Thoughts Betrayed at basic, and then strikes with his hands.

He gets hit with First Strike by the Muddled Vampire Hunter and goes to
torpor.

Does the Muddled Vampire Hunter get hit by the damage from the Thoughts
Betrayed? Why or Why not?

Cheers,

Andrew.

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
In article <91rvt3$art$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,

hel...@my-deja.com wrote:
> Scenario:
>
> Samson has 2 blood, and is attacked by a Muddled Vampire Hunter.
>
> He plays Thoughts Betrayed at basic, and then strikes with his hands.
>
> He gets hit with First Strike by the Muddled Vampire Hunter and
> goes to torpor.
>
> Does the Muddled Vampire Hunter get hit by the damage from
> the Thoughts Betrayed?

No.

Card Text:
Thoughts Betrayed [DS, SW]
Cardtype: Combat
Cost: 2 blood
Discipline: Dominate
Only usable before range is determined on the first round. Opposing
minion takes an additional 1 damage in the first round of combat during
strike resolution. (S) Only usable before range is determined on the
first round. Opposing minion cannot play any strike cards for the
duration of this combat.

> Why or Why not?

The combat never reaches the strike resolution phase
for Samson's strike, so the damage will never be done.
The combat ends when Samson goes to torpor during the
resolution of the Muddled Vampire Hunter's strike.

Same thing if Muddles is attacking a vampire with a retainer
that does damage, if the vampire goes to torpor because of
the first strike, the retainer will do no damage that combat.

See the Rules Team Ruling from 11/09/1994 quoted here:

"The damage is done during normal damage dealing, so a Combat
Ends will stop it, as will sending its controller to torpor
during first strike. [RTR 19941109]"

This was issued for the damage from Wolf Companion, and
all retainers follow it. Thoughts Betrayed does damage
at the same time retainers do their damage, so the damage
will not be done if a SCE happens, or if the playing vampire
goes to torpor during first strike.

Carpe Noctem.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


First Strike doesn't set up two resolution phases.

It merely "sets up" a strike that will resolve before normal
strikes (and, therefore, before effects that occurs during
normal strike resolution).

If you like, you can treat the time in which First Strikes
resolve as a separate strike resolution phase, but that phase
is always there (and usually skipped).

First Strike is described on page 41.
The fact that "during strike resolution" effects occur during
normal strike resolution (as opposed to first strike resolution)
is not spelled out there, however. It is merely assumed as a
default.

Messages.Body:
In article <91tmdg$lnh$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,

Cheers. I perceive a little ambiguity in the process of strike
resolutions here. If there is a seperate first strike resolution
phase, then everything is clear. However, you mention that while we
can treat it as if this is the case, in reality there is only one
strike resolution phase.

If there is only one strike resolution phase, then you would expect
that effects that cause a damage during the strike resolution phase
will occur regardless of whether the vampire who played the card to
cause the effect is still around to resolve their actual strike or
not. The damage from Thoughts Betrayed is nothing to do with the
actual strike of the minion who plays it. So, even if they do not get
to resolve their strike, if the (one) strike resolution phase is
entered, the damage from the Thoughts Betrayed should still be in
effect.

Similar to the damage from Drawing out the Beast, which takes effect at
the end of the round regardless of whether the minion who played the
card is in torpor or not.

Thanks to the previous message in the thread, I realise that you have
ruled on the damage from retainers like Wolf Companion not being
effective if the retaining minion is sent to torpor with first strike,
however, there is more of an intuitive link between the timing of the
strike of the retaining minion and the damage of the wolf companion,
than there is between the strike of the minion and the damage from
Thoughts Betrayed. I hate resorting to words like "intuitive link",
but there are a few assumptions going on here.

Any clarifications would be appreciated.
